strings.about.title: About these insights
strings.about.not_causal: These are associations in your own check-ins, not a cause. Nothing here can tell you that one thing made another happen.
strings.about.disclaimer: Manovia is a self-help companion. It is not therapy, it cannot diagnose, and these numbers are not a measurement of your mental health.

about.limitations: A tag says a thing was on your mind, not whether it went well. "Sleep" covers a good night and a bad one; a difference on sleep days is a difference between two kinds of day you labelled the same way.
Your check-ins are not a random sample of your life. A day worth writing down is usually a day that stood out, which tilts every average here.

Small samples move a lot. Nothing is reported until each side has at least 5 check-ins, the difference is at least 0.4 points on the 1–5 scale, and it survives a permutation test at a threshold corrected for how many comparisons were run.
Two things that show up together often have a third thing behind them. An exam week can carry both less sleep and a lower mood.
When you check in is part of what these numbers say. Somebody who only writes at night will look like a night person.
These averages are yours. There is no typical score, and no number on this page is good or bad.
about.methods: Rolling average: the mean of the check-ins inside the trailing 7 or 30 local days, always shown with the count it was made from.
Trend: the last 7 days compared with the 7 before them, needing at least 7 check-ins in each, and called a direction only when a bootstrap interval for the change does not include zero.

Tag comparisons: the mean with a tag minus the mean without it, tested with a 2000-draw permutation test at 0.05 divided by the number of comparisons in the family, plus a 2000-draw percentile bootstrap interval.
Time of day and weekday: one omnibus permutation test per grouping; the extreme groups are named only when each holds at least 5 check-ins and they differ by at least 0.4 points.
Every resampling draw is seeded; the same check-ins always produce the same numbers and the same sentences.
